_provenance.note: Hand-authored for NARR-1 (the narrative-eval CE wedge, SPEC_NARRATIVE_EVAL). A non-clinical domain: auditing AI-rewritten interactive-fiction scenes (Lenador StoryWorld) against the enhancement prompt's own authored contract + narrative judge lenses. Internally consistent with taxonomy_snapshot.json — every gradeable flag's code is in a tier AND in exactly one judge's lens; the two Tier-1 never-events have an owning role. NARR-3 attaches the 3 P0 deterministic FLOOR executors (bracket_leak/length_violation/silent_degradation, defined in floors.py) via verification_contracts; the floors are pure-stdlib in_process, so the grade path still never reaches :8002. The prose is needle-free (no HIPAA/patient/medication/dosage/allergy/clinical/SOAP/escalation/consent/transcript wording) so render_role_questions emits a clean non-clinical judge prompt.

flags.definition: The generated scene leaks an instruction marker — text in square brackets that is an input to the model and must never reach the reader.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: Square brackets that are legitimately part of the authored story body (e.g. a quoted sign). The scene is clean of any marker text.
flags.when_to_use: 1) The output contains '[READER FEELING ...]' or any bracketed directive. 2) A '[square brackets]' instruction fragment appears mid-prose.

flags.definition: The scene was filtered, truncated, or fell back to a baseline generation while still being reported as a complete, final result.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: The scene is a complete generation, or a fallback that is clearly labelled as such. A deliberate, disclosed baseline.
flags.when_to_use: 1) A content-filtered generation was silently replaced by the baseline text and shipped as final. 2) A truncated output is presented as a finished scene.

flags.definition: The added preamble introduces an action or state that contradicts the authored scene body that immediately follows it.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: The preamble stays interior (thought, sensation) and leaves the body's opening action intact. A reasonable bridge that the body then continues.
flags.when_to_use: 1) The preamble has the character walking away while the body opens with them speaking in place. 2) The preamble resolves tension the body still treats as unresolved.

flags.definition: The added preamble is not the required length (3-4 sentences).
flags.when_NOT_to_use: The preamble is 3 or 4 sentences as specified.
flags.when_to_use: 1) The preamble is a single run-on sentence. 2) The preamble runs to six or more sentences.

flags.definition: The narration slips into first or second person in a story whose established voice is third person.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: First/second person inside quoted dialogue. The story's own established voice is first person.
flags.when_to_use: 1) The preamble narrates 'I felt my pulse jump' in a third-person story. 2) The narration addresses the reader as 'you' outside dialogue.

flags.definition: The output is not in the session's stated language.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: A handful of established proper nouns or loanwords that belong to the story world. The output is wholly in the session language.
flags.when_to_use: 1) An English-session scene drifts into another language mid-paragraph. 2) The preamble is generated in the wrong language entirely.

flags.definition: The scene's content is not appropriate for the story's stated audience mode (adult, youth, or children).
flags.when_NOT_to_use: The content matches the stated mode's expectations. Mild peril appropriate to the audience.
flags.when_to_use: 1) Graphic content in a children mode scene. 2) Content pitched far below an adult mode's register in a way that breaks the experience.

flags.definition: The scene violates the story's established theme, tone, or lesson.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: A deliberate, earned tonal beat that still serves the theme. The scene stays within the story's mythic/adventurous register.
flags.when_to_use: 1) A flippant, comedic register in a mythic, courage-themed story. 2) A scene that undercuts the stated lesson.

flags.definition: The prose leans on overused tension or fear cliches the enhancement contract asks the writer to avoid.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: A fresh, specific image even if it touches a familiar feeling. One incidental common phrase.
flags.when_to_use: 1) 'Her heart pounded in her chest' as the tension image. 2) Stacked stock cliches for fear or suspense.

flags.definition: The scene reuses an image or metaphor already used in an earlier scene this session.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: A deliberate, recognisable motif used for effect. A common word that is not a distinctive image.
flags.when_to_use: 1) The same 'humming in her teeth' image appears in two scenes. 2) A distinctive metaphor from an earlier preamble is repeated verbatim.

flags.definition: The scene ignores or contradicts the reader's stated choices or bridge answers.
flags.when_NOT_to_use: The scene honours the reader's stated emotion/choice, or stays neutral where no answer constrains it.
flags.when_to_use: 1) The reader answered 'Confidence' but the preamble writes them as panicked. 2) The scene contradicts a choice the reader made at a branch point.

questions.text: Does the scene contain NO text in square brackets (no leaked instruction marker)?
Is the added preamble 3-4 sentences and in the same language as the rest of the story?
Does the narration stay in the story's established third-person point of view?
Is the prose free of overused tension cliches and of images already used in earlier scenes?
Was the scene produced by a complete generation, not a filtered or truncated output silently presented as final?
Is the content appropriate for the story's stated audience mode (adult, youth, or children)?
Does the added preamble stay consistent with the authored scene body it precedes, introducing nothing that contradicts it?
Does the scene stay faithful to the story's theme, tone, and lesson?
Does the scene honour the reader's stated choices and bridge answers?

verification_contracts.question: Is the shipped scene free of any leaked instruction marker (bracketed directive text)?
Was the scene a complete generation, not a non-stop result silently demoted to the baseline yet shipped as final?
Is the added preamble within the required 3-4 sentence band?
